Otherwise, dispatch the task reviewer with the path.
315	
316	**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.
317	
318	**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.
319	
320	**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
321	1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
322	2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
323	3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
324	4. If the plan itself is wrong, stop and escalate to your human partner — the plan text, what it breaks, and the correction you would make
325	
326	**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.
327	
328	If the implementer asks questions — before starting or mid-task — answer
329	clearly and completely, provide additional context if needed, and don't
330	rush it into implementation.
331	
332	### 3. Review the task
333	
334	Per-task reviews are task-scoped gates. The broad review happens once, at the
335	final whole-branch review. Never skip the task review, and never accept a
336	report missing either verdict — spec compliance AND task quality are both
337	required. Implementer self-review never replaces the task review; both are
338	needed. Note the task's effective risk tier as you go (see Risk Tiers,
339	below) — the Claude task review always runs, but the tier decides whether
340	step 4's per-task Codex gate does.
341	
342	- Hand the reviewer its diff as a file: run this skill's
343	  `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD` — it prints
344	  `wrote <path>: <N> commit(s), <N> bytes`, so take the path from that line
345	  and pass it to the reviewer (or, without bash: `git log --oneline`,
346	  `git diff --stat`, and `git diff -U10` for the range, redirected to one
347	  uniquely named file). The output never enters your own context, and the reviewer sees
348	  the commit list, stat summary, and full diff with context in one Read
349	  call. Use the BASE you recorded before dispatching the implementer —
350	  never `HEAD~1`, which silently truncates multi-commit tasks. Never
351	  dispatch a task reviewer without a diff file.
352	- **Reviewer inputs:** the task reviewer gets three paths — the same brief
353	  file, the report file, and the review package — plus the global
354	  constraints that bind the task. Write those global constraints to a small
355	  file alongside the brief and report: the per-task Codex gate takes the
356	  same file as its global-constraints handoff.
357	- The global-constraints block you hand the reviewer is its attention
358	  lens. Copy the binding requirements verbatim from the plan's Global
359	  Constraints section or the spec: exact values, exact formats, and the
360	  stated relationships between components ("same layout as X", "matches
361	  Y"). The reviewer's template already carries the process rules (YAGNI,
362	  test hygiene, review method) — the constraints block is for what THIS
363	  project's spec demands.
364	- Do not add open-ended directives like "check all uses" or "run race tests
365	  if useful" without a concrete, task-specific reason
366	- Do not ask a reviewer to re-run tests the implementer already ran on the
367	  same code — the implementer's report carries the test evidence
368	- Do not pre-judge findings for the reviewer — never instruct a reviewer to
369	  ignore or not flag a specific issue. If you believe a finding would be a
370	  false positive, let the reviewer raise it and adjudicate it in the review
371	  loop. If the prompt you are writing contains "do not flag," "don't treat X
372	  as a defect," "at most Minor," or "the plan chose" — stop: you are
373	  pre-judging, usually to spare yourself a review loop. When the plan supplies
374	  example code, weaknesses in that code are fair review targets — the example
375	  was a starting point, not evidence that its weaknesses were chosen.
376	The task reviewer may report "⚠️ Cannot verify from diff" items — requirements
377	that live in unchanged code or span tasks. These do not block the rest of the
378	review, but you must resolve each one yourself before marking the task
379	complete: you hold the plan and cross-task context the reviewer
380	lacks. If you confirm an item is a real gap, treat it as a failed spec
381	review — it enters the fix loop with the other findings.
382	
383	Template: [task-reviewer-prompt.md](task-reviewer-prompt.md)
384	
385	### 4. The fix loop
386	
387	The loop triggers when the review reports spec ❌, any Critical or Important
388	finding, a ⚠️ item you confirmed as a real gap, or a blocking finding from
389	the per-task Codex gate below.
390	
391	Task-reviewer findings are claims too. The resumed implementer verifies
392	each finding against the code before fixing it
393	(hyperpowers:receiving-code-review); a finding is declined only as
394	refuted or corrected with file:line evidence, which the controller
395	records in the ledger; a confirmed finding is fixed or carried open; a
396	finding nobody can settle stays open and counts against the round cap.
397	
398	Before the loop starts, two routes leave it immediately:
399	
400	- Record Minor findings in the progress ledger as you go
401	  (`Task <N>: minor (deferred): <one-liner>`), and point the final
402	  whole-branch review at that list so it can triage which must be fixed
403	  before merge. A roll-up nobody reads is a silent discard. Minor findings
404	  never enter the loop.
405	- A finding labeled plan-mandated — or any finding that conflicts with what
406	  the plan's text requires — is your human partner's decision: present the
407	  finding and the plan text beside it and ask which governs. Do not dismiss
408	  the finding because the plan mandates it, and do not dispatch a fix that
409	  contradicts the plan without asking.
410	
411	Everything else enters the loop — the Claude task reviewer's blocking
412	findings and the per-task Codex gate's blocking findings alike. They are ONE
413	loop with ONE shared cap of **five rounds per task**: the gate does not run
414	a count of its own. A fix round is one fix dispatch — or one
415	controller-applied de-minimis fix — plus one scoped re-review.
416	
417	**Rounds 1-3 — resume the original implementer.** Send it the open findings
418	verbatim. Its context is intact: it knows the task, the code, and its own
419	choices. If your harness cannot send another message to a live subagent,
420	dispatch a fresh implementer carrying the brief path, the report-file path,
421	and the findings — the report file is the persistent memory either way.
422	
423	**Rounds 4-5 — dispatch a fresh takeover implementer on a more capable
424	model** (per Model Selection), with the brief path, the report-file path,
425	the open findings, and this framing: "A prior implementer attempted this
426	task [N] times; you own it now. Read the report file for what was tried." A
427	loop that survives three resumes usually means the implementer cannot see
428	its own problem — fresh eyes and a capability bump in one move.
429	
430	**Every round, either way:** the implementer fixes, re-runs the tests
431	covering the amended code, appends its fix report to the same report file,
432	and returns the short contract. Before re-dispatching the reviewer, confirm
433	the fix report contains the covering tests, the command run, and the
434	output; dispatch the re-review once all three are present. That
435	precondition covers the findings the round fixed; a round that declines
436	every finding is defined below. Name the covering test files in the fix
437	message — a one-line fix does not need the whole suite. The per-task loop
438	resumes an implementer rather than dispatching a fixer, so it never uses
439	[fix-subagent-prompt.md](fix-subagent-prompt.md) — that template belongs to
440	the final review's one fix wave.
441	
442	**The re-review is scoped.** Run `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD`
443	where FIX_BASE is the head the previous review saw, and dispatch
444	[re-review-prompt.md](re-review-prompt.md) with the findings list, the
445	brief, the report file, and the printed diff path. The re-reviewer verdicts
446	each finding ADDRESSED, NOT ADDRESSED, or DECLINED — a refuted or corrected
447	finding whose file:line evidence the re-reviewer has confirmed; an unconfirmed
448	decline stays NOT ADDRESSED — and flags new breakage in the fix diff only. The
449	controller records each DECLINED finding in the ledger with its evidence. New
450	Critical/Important breakage in the fix diff joins the open findings list.
451	Out-of-scope observations go to the ledger as deferred minors — they never
452	extend the loop. Every round in this loop ends with the scoped re-review —
453	never a full task-reviewer re-run, whatever the finding's origin.
454	
455	**A round that declines every finding changes no code.** There is no fix
456	diff and no covering test to confirm; the implementer's report is the
457	artifact, carrying for each finding the refuted or corrected evidence at
458	file:line. Skip `scripts/review-package` for that round — its range is
459	empty — and dispatch the scoped re-review with the findings list, the brief,
460	the report, and the previous review's package path, so the re-reviewer
461	verdicts each finding DECLINED or NOT ADDRESSED from the evidence alone. The
462	covering-tests precondition applies only to findings that were fixed. Record
463	the round as `(0 addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open)`; a NOT ADDRESSED verdict
464	keeps that finding open and the round counts toward the cap as usual.
465	
466	**After each round,** append to the ledger:
467	`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 (<X> addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`
468	
469	Never fix findings yourself in the controller session — your context stays
470	clean for coordination, and controller fixes skip review. One narrow
471	exception: a fix fully specified by the finding itself — exact file, exact
472	lines, exact replacement, no judgment left — touching at most 3 lines in
473	one file with no new logic, may be controller-applied — one finding per
474	reach; a round holding two such findings is not de minimis. The exception
475	waives nothing else: it consumes a fix round and ends in the same scoped
476	re-review; the controller applies the edit and runs the fix's covering
477	command FIRST — a failure means the fix was not de minimis: revert the
478	edit, spend no round, and go back to the round's own rule — then commits
479	the verified fix (the re-review packages committed diffs — an
480	uncommitted fix hands it nothing) and appends the fix report — the
481	command, its output, and a diff summary — to the task's report file
482	itself, exactly as an implementer would. Its ledger line keeps the
483	fix-round schema with the marker inside it:
484	`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 controller-applied (de minimis) (<X> addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`.
485	Reaching for it twice in the same task means the findings are not de
486	minimis — go back to the round's own rule: resume the implementer at
487	rounds 1-3, dispatch the takeover at rounds 4-5.
488	
489	**Codex Review Gate (Claude Code only).** When running under Claude Code, add
490	a Codex **code** review gate at two points — here, per task, and once more
491	at the final whole-branch review — following
492	[../requesting-code-review/codex-review-gate.md](../requesting-code-review/codex-review-gate.md).
493	Probe once per skill run and reuse the result; if Codex is absent, emit the
494	no-Codex notice once and run both gates as no-ops.
495	
496	- **Per task:** after the task reviewer approves (spec ✅ and quality approved) and
497	  before marking the task complete, run the gate (standard/high effective tiers; an effective-low task skips it per Risk Tiers below, recording the tier-skip event instead) using the per-task code recipe
498	  with `--base <the task BASE you recorded before dispatching the implementer>`.
499	  Provide the task brief path, implementer report path, review-package path, and
500	  the global-constraints file you wrote in step 3. The gate's dossier `--adjudications` inputs carry the plan's `**Spec:**` file path beside any spec-gate ledger, so the reviewer is handed the binding authority instead of inferring it.
501	- **Rounds are shared, not stacked.** Blocking findings from this gate enter
502	  the same five-round loop above, at the next round number — the gate has no
503	  separate Codex ceiling of its own. The task's fix-round budget is five,
504	  shared across Claude-reviewer rounds and Codex-gate rounds. Three mechanics
505	  keep that single budget honest:
506	
507	  1. **One `GATE_DIR` for this task's whole gate lifecycle.** Create it at
508	     the task's first gate invocation and reuse that same dir for every
509	     Codex re-round of this task — the gate doc's §3 contract, "Use one
510	     `GATE_DIR` for the whole gate." `gate-round`'s counter lives in that
511	     dir, so it counts exactly this task's gate rounds and nothing else.
512	     When the `GATE_DIR` is first created, record it in the progress ledger
513	     as one line `Task N gate dir: <path>`; on resume (or any later Codex
514	     re-round), reuse the ledgered path instead of creating a new one; if
515	     the ledgered dir no longer exists (cache purged), treat the task's
516	     prior gate rounds as unknown and fail closed: do not assume zero —
517	     reconstruct the consumed-round count from the ledger's fix-round
518	     entries and, if gate rounds cannot be established, surface via BLOCKED
519	     rather than restarting the count.
520	  2. **Let the counter do the arithmetic.** `gate-round` compares its LOCAL
521	     count — gate rounds only, monotonic within the `GATE_DIR` — against a
522	     ceiling, so the ceiling must leave gate rounds out; they are already in
523	     that count. Pass `--consumed <NON-gate fix rounds this task has consumed
524	     so far>` (all fix/re-review rounds, whatever the finding's origin — the
525	     gate's own invocation rounds are excluded only because `gate-round`'s
526	     counter already holds them) and the script derives the ceiling from the
527	     shared five-round cap itself. Recompute the consumed count at each call:
528	     non-gate rounds may land between gate rounds. Do not hand-compute
529	     `--ceiling` for a task gate — that is how twenty measured task gates
530	     recorded ceilings of 1, 2, 6, and 7, two of which the cap makes
531	     impossible. `--consumed` cannot express them.
532	  3. **A spent cap is BLOCKED, not a gate round.** When the task's consumed
533	     rounds already total five, `--consumed 5` yields a ceiling of zero and
534	     the gate backstops on its first call. That is the fail-closed floor, not
535	     the intended path: check before calling, and when the cap is spent follow
536	     the breaker below and surface the task as BLOCKED rather than spending a
537	     gate invocation to learn it.
538	
539	  The invariant in one line: **local gate rounds + non-gate fix rounds ≤ 5**,
540	  enforced because `gate-round` blocks (verdict `backstop`) the moment its
541	  local count would exceed the ceiling. Count every round the
542	  gate runs against the task's shared budget — each gate round consumes one
543	  of the five, exactly like a reviewer round. After a Codex-triggered fix,
544	  the scoped re-review verifies it; the gate re-runs only once that
545	  re-review verdicts every finding ADDRESSED or DECLINED.
546	
547	**The breaker.** When round 5's re-review — or a per-task Codex gate at the
548	spent cap — still leaves blocking findings open, stop dispatching. The task
549	does not silently continue and nothing is parked on your own authority:
550	surface the open findings to your human partner as BLOCKED, each with the
551	rounds already spent, what was tried, and the evidence. Ledger it:
552	`Task <N>: BLOCKED at cap — <finding one-liners>`. They decide what happens
553	next.
554	
555	### 5. Complete the task
556	
557	When the review comes back clean — the task reviewer approved, every
558	fix-loop finding is addressed or declined, and the per-task Codex gate
559	approved or was skipped by tier — append the completion line to the ledger
560	in the same message as your other bookkeeping:
561	
562	- `Task <N>: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, review clean)`
563	
564	Then mark the task's todo complete, where you keep todos, and move on.
565	Never move to the next task while the review has open Critical/Important
566	issues.
567	
568	## Risk Tiers (per-task Codex gate applicability)
569	
570	Tiers are `low`, `standard`, `high`, declared per task in the plan. A task
571	skips the per-task Codex gate only when all three hold: declared low, the
572	plan's own Codex gate actually reviewed the plan, and no escalation trigger
573	fired at any point during execution. That skip is recorded durably. An
574	unreviewed low tier — plan gate skipped, degraded, or outcome unknown —
575	executes as standard, and a task demoted that way runs the full train and
576	records NO tier-skip event. The Claude task reviewer and the final
577	whole-branch train never tier off. When any task did skip, write
578	`tier-skips.md` in this plan's workspace; Final Review hands its path to the
579	final reviewer and the final Codex gate. The escalation triggers, the
580	fallback rules, and the exact ledger line shape are in
581	[risk-tiers.md](risk-tiers.md) — read it before dispatching any task declared
582	low.
583	
584	## Final Review
585	
586	The final whole-branch review gets a package too: run
587	`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE MERGE_BASE HEAD` (MERGE_BASE = the commit the
588	branch started from, e.g. `git merge-base main HEAD`) — take the path from the
589	`wrote <path>: ...` line and include it in the final review dispatch, so the
590	final reviewer reads one file instead of re-deriving the branch diff with git
591	commands. Dispatch
592	on the most capable available model (see Model Selection), using
593	hyperpowers:requesting-code-review's
594	[code-reviewer.md](../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md). Point it at
595	the ledger's deferred-minor lines — and at `tier-skips.md`, if any task
596	skipped its per-task gate — so it can triage which must be fixed before
597	merge.
598	
599	If the final whole-branch review returns findings, dispatch ONE fix subagent
600	with the complete findings list — not one fixer per finding. Compose the
601	dispatch from [fix-subagent-prompt.md](fix-subagent-prompt.md).
602	Per-finding fixers each rebuild context and re-run suites; a real
603	session's final-review fix wave cost more than all its tasks combined.
604	Then run exactly one scoped re-review of the fix wave
605	(`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD` over the fix range,
606	[re-review-prompt.md](re-review-prompt.md) using its Final-wave usage note).
607	There is no second fix wave: anything the re-review leaves open — and any
608	finding that conflicts with the plan's text — goes to your human partner
609	with the evidence, as BLOCKED, when finishing-a-development-branch presents
610	the options.
611	
612	**Codex Review Gate — final whole-branch (Claude Code only).** After the final code-reviewer
613	subagent and its fix wave, and before hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch,
614	run the gate using the final whole-branch code recipe with `--base <branch
615	merge-base, e.g. git merge-base main HEAD>`. Provide the branch
616	review-package path, plan or requirements path, the Minor findings ledger if
617	present, and the tier-skip summary if any task skipped. The final dossier passes the plan's `**Spec:**` file as a `--doc` input beside the plan, and carries the tier-skip summary among its `--adjudications`. Resolve blocking
618	findings with one fix subagent carrying the complete list, per this
619	section's existing guidance, before finishing. After any Codex-triggered
620	final-review fix, re-run the final code-reviewer before re-running the final
621	Codex gate.
622	
623	Unlike the per-task gate, the final gate keeps a ceiling of its own: the
624	gate's convergence stop-rule and per-gate backstop bound this loop (code
625	gates use a code-gate backstop of 3 rounds). If the backstop is hit with
626	unresolved blocking findings, surface them to your human partner rather than
627	looping.
628	
629	## Finish
630	
631	When the final whole-branch review is clean and its fixes are merged:
632	
633	1. **Delete this plan's workspace** with `rm -rf <workspace>` (the path
634	   `scripts/sdd-dir <plan>` prints — the directory holding this plan's
635	   ledger, briefs, reports, review packages, and tier-skip summary).
636	2. **Verify deletion** with `test ! -d "<workspace>"` to confirm it is gone.
637	
638	A clean finish that leaves the workspace behind is an INCOMPLETE finish —
639	"keeping it for reference" is not an option; the repo's commits are the
640	durable record. Sibling directories belong to other plans; leave them
641	alone. The 14-day reclaim in `scripts/sdd-dir` is only the backstop for
642	sessions that never got here.
643	
644	Use hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch.
645	
646	## Common Rationalizations
647	
648	The excuses that show up mid-run and what is actually true:
649	[common-rationalizations.md](common-rationalizations.md). Read it the moment you
650	catch yourself justifying a shortcut.
651	
652	## Example Workflow
653	
654	A complete worked run, dispatch through finish:
655	[example-workflow.md](example-workflow.md).

1	===== gate-preflight
2	## 1. Preflight availability
3	
4	Run the preflight by its absolute path inside the installed plugin
5	(`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is set by Claude Code to this plugin's install
6	directory):
7	
8	```bash
9	bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/codex-preflight"
10	```
11	
12	(When working inside a hyperpowers dev checkout rather than an installed
13	plugin, `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is unset; run
14	`bash skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/codex-preflight` from the repo
15	root instead. If it is unset in an *installed-plugin* session, resolve the
16	newest install: `ls -d ~/.claude/plugins/cache/hyperpowers/hyperpowers/*/ | sort -V | tail -1`.)
17	
18	It prints one JSON line. Branch on `.status`:
19	
20	- **`"ok"`** — a Codex review can run. Capture `.codexPath` as `CODEX_PATH`
21	  and `.codexVersion` as `CODEX_VERSION` (report it in the §6 hand-back).
22	  The JSON field paths in §4b's payloads are verified against codex-plugin-cc
23	  **1.0.5–1.0.6**; on another version, confirm a field exists in the actual
24	  payload before relying on it.
25	- **`"not-installed"`** — emit the **No-Codex notice** (§2) and continue the
26	  skill unchanged. Do not treat this as an error.
27	- **`"not-ready"`** — the plugin is installed but Codex is not ready
28	  (`.reason` says why: not authenticated, CLI missing, transient handshake
29	  failure that outlasted retries). Tell the user once:
30	  "Note [status: not-ready]: codex-plugin-cc is installed but not ready (<.reason>), so this review will run without an additional Codex review." Then continue exactly
31	  as the §2 degrade path.
32	- **`"stale-broker"`** — the plugin is installed but this repo's companion
33	  broker is dead (its temp dir was likely purged mid-session; the session-
34	  start janitor clears these at startup/compact, so this means it died
35	  since). Tell the user once, quoting `.recovery` verbatim:
36	  "Note [status: stale-broker]: the Codex companion broker for this repo is stale, so this review will run without a Codex review. To restore Codex for the next gate, run this in a terminal: <.recovery>" — then continue as the §2 degrade path.
37	  The next gate re-runs preflight and picks the recovery up automatically.
38	- **Non-zero exit** (internal failure — the preflight tooling itself broke) —
39	  degrade exactly like §2, but with its own attribution. Tell the user once:
40	  "Note [status: preflight-error]: the Codex preflight failed (<stderr summary>), so this review will run without an additional Codex review."
41	  Do not treat this as an error and do not claim Codex is not installed.
42	
43	**Record every degrade durably.** Whenever a gate proceeds on a degrade
44	branch (`not-installed`, `not-ready`, `stale-broker`, `preflight-error`),
45	append a ledger event before continuing (the approach gate alone is exempt: no ledger token, no §6 on its route — it proceeds per §2) — document gates:
46	
47	```bash
48	bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/ungated-ledger" append --class degraded-gate --gate <spec|plan> --status <token> --note "<one line; include the task brief / plan path if one exists — the sweep uses it as a breadcrumb>"
49	```
50	
51	Code gates additionally record the exact range that will ship unreviewed:
52	
53	```bash
54	bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/ungated-ledger" append --class degraded-gate --gate <task|final|adhoc> --base <the gate's BASE sha> --head "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --status <token> --note "<one line; include the task brief / plan path if one exists — the sweep uses it as a breadcrumb>"
55	```
56	
57	`--gate-dir` is omitted here on purpose: preflight runs BEFORE §3 creates
58	`GATE_DIR`, and `gateDir` is a forensic breadcrumb only — class-1 preflight
59	events legitimately carry `gateDir:null`. If a `GATE_DIR` already exists
60	for this gate when the degrade occurs, passing `--gate-dir "$GATE_DIR"` is
61	welcome but never required.
62	
63	If the append itself fails, say so loudly in the §6 hand-back ("ungated
64	event could NOT be recorded — note this manually") and continue — a
65	bookkeeping failure never blocks the gate.
66	
67	**Re-surface pending work on healthy preflight.** When `.status` is `ok`,

252	**Code reviews — launch detached, watch in the foreground.** The three code
253	recipes below all use `adversarial-review`, which the companion runs as one
254	long turn (typically 2–5 minutes, sometimes 10+). Never run it as a plain
255	blocking shell call: if the harness command timeout kills that call, the
256	companion dies mid-turn and never writes a terminal job state — the job is
257	orphaned as `running`, `result` refuses it forever, and the verdict is
258	unrecoverable except by a full re-run. Instead:
259	
260	1. **Launch in the background.** Run the recipe command with the shell tool's
261	   run-in-background option (not `nohup`, not a trailing `&`). The detached
262	   process survives watcher timeouts and always persists a terminal result;
263	   its captured output also holds the full `--json` payload as a fallback.
264	2. **Capture the job id.** Immediately run
265	   `node "$CODEX_PATH/scripts/codex-companion.mjs" status --json` in the
266	   foreground and take the `id` of the newest `.running[]` entry with
267	   `jobClass: "review"`; if the job has not registered yet, re-run the status
268	   call after a couple of seconds.
269	3. **Watch in the foreground — never idle.** Block on one shell call (timeout 600000 ms) that watches every job id at once:
270	   `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/gate-wait" <job-id>...` with `CODEX_PATH` exported, outside the shell sandbox like every companion command;
271	   it re-reads every job without blocking, waits on one at a time in slices of at most 30 s, and returns when all are terminal (exit 0, last line `all-terminal`) or after its 480 s budget (exit 2, last line `running: <ids>`).
272	   On exit 2, immediately issue the next `gate-wait` over the ids still running. On exit 1 from a usage error, fix the call and re-run; on exit 1 for a job it could not read (last line `unreadable: <ids>`; the `running:` line before it, when present, lists the ids still running; stderr names the cause), first check that lens's captured launch output for its `--json` payload, then run one `status <job-id> --json` for that job: if it is still unreadable, that review is incomplete per §4b, with at most one relaunch if the failure looked transient; keep watching the ids still running with `gate-wait`.
273	   Never call `status <job-id> --wait` yourself; it is the primitive `gate-wait` runs for you.
274	   While the review runs, the session must always be inside one of these
275	   blocking watch calls — never `sleep`, never fire-and-forget and move on.
276	   This keeps the session visibly working in harness UIs and the wait
277	   interruptible, while the review itself is immune to any single call being
278	   killed.
279	4. **Read the verdict.** Once `.job.status` is terminal, run `node "$CODEX_PATH/scripts/codex-companion.mjs" result <job-id> --json`: write the full `result <job-id> --json` output to a file inside `GATE_DIR` and run `verdict-normalize` on it; the raw review text for reading findings remains at `.storedJob.result.rawOutput`.

335	## 4. Interpret — severity mapping
336	
337	Map Codex severities to Hyperpowers' vocabulary:
338	
339	| Codex | Hyperpowers | Blocking? |
340	|-------|-------------|-----------|
341	| critical | Critical | yes |
342	| high | Important | yes |
343	| medium / low | Minor | no |
344	
345	**Blocking = Critical + Important.** Minor findings are noted, not fixed in the loop.
346	
347	## 4b. Completion check — incomplete is not approval
348	
349	A Codex result has three outcomes, not two: *approve*, *blocking findings*, and
350	**incomplete**. An incomplete result carries no verdict and must never be read as
351	approval or as "no findings."
352	
353	**Mechanical normalization — the only approval authority.** Write the
354	captured result (the foreground `task` stdout, or `result <job-id> --json`
355	output) to a file inside `GATE_DIR`, then run:
356	
357	```bash
358	bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/verdict-normalize" "$GATE_DIR/<captured-output-file>"
359	```
360	
361	Round-1 captures (every lens, dossier-backed or fallback) add `--require-coverage` to this command; re-review rounds run it without the flag.
362	
363	**Round-1 lens captures.** Normalize every round-1 capture with `verdict-normalize --require-coverage` — the coverage floor is part of the approval authority. Capture each lens's output to its own file in `GATE_DIR` and normalize each:
364	
365	```bash
366	bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/verdict-normalize" --require-coverage "$GATE_DIR/lens-<name>-capture"
367	```
368	
369	The round's verdict merges fail-closed: ALL lenses `approved` → the round is approved. ANY lens
370	`incomplete` — after per-lens recovery (the bounded re-fetch below, plus at most one relaunch of
371	THAT lens if the failure looked transient) — → the round is incomplete: surviving lenses' blocking
372	findings still enter the round ledger as actionable work, but nothing approves. Otherwise → blocking.
373	Deduplicate findings into the ONE round ledger: same file/section + same defect = ONE merged entry
374	— never one entry per lens — written once with every reporting lens's tag appended, e.g. `[lens:
375	correctness] [lens: contracts-and-integration]`; every entry carries its source tag `[lens: <name>]`
376	(plus `[out-of-lane]` where the lens said so). Re-review rounds normalize their single capture
377	WITHOUT the flag, exactly as today. Two findings are the same defect when they cite the same file and the same offending code AND describe the same failure: the same violated requirement, trigger, and bad outcome. Titles and line numbers do not decide it: each lens phrases a title differently and line numbers drift, but the quoted evidence and the failure do not. Location alone is not identity: one fragment can carry two independent defects, and those stay separate. When entries merge, the strictest severity survives.
378	
379	Its tri-state `.result` is the review outcome: `approved`, `blocking`, or
380	`incomplete`. Only a `verdict-normalize` result of `approved` counts as
381	approval — never your own reading of the raw output, and never the absence
382	of output. On `approved` reached through a `needs-attention` verdict, the capture carries medium/low notes: read them and record each in the round ledger (and in the skill's Minor ledger, if it keeps one) before treating the round as converged. On `blocking`, read the raw findings text as usual to do the
383	fixing; normalization gates only the decision. On `incomplete`, follow the
384	recovery steps below, re-capture, and re-normalize; if it remains
385	`incomplete`, surface "Codex review did not complete — not an approval."
386	
387	**Why this matters (grounding).** Within the companion, `adversarial-review` is
388	**foreground-only**: `handleReviewCommand` always calls `runForegroundCommand`,
389	and the review command's own `--wait`/`--background` flags are parsed but
390	ignored. The background path for code gates therefore comes from the harness
391	side — the detached launch in recipe-code.md — and it is required, not optional. If the
392	review is instead run as a plain blocking call and the harness command timeout
393	kills it, the companion process dies mid-turn and never writes a terminal job
394	state: the job record stays `running` with a dead worker, `status <job-id>
395	--wait` burns its full deadline, and `result` refuses forever. No recovery can
396	conjure the verdict in that case; prevention (the detached launch) is the
397	mitigation. The 240 s `waitTimedOut` deadline belongs to `status --wait` —
398	hitting it is not a review failure, just the cue to issue the next watch call.
399	
400	**A review result is incomplete when any hold:**
401	
402	- the background launch exits non-zero, or its job never appears in
403	  `status --json`,
404	- the recipe-code.md watch cap is reached with `.job.status` still `queued`/`running`,
405	- a foreground call (document review) is aborted by the harness command timeout
406	  before returning, or exits non-zero,
407	- the `--json` payload has no terminal verdict / no structured `result` payload
408	  (`.storedJob.result.result` null — check `.storedJob.result.parseError` for a
409	  schema-compliance failure that still exits 0),
410	- the rendered text reads as in-progress ("still verifying", "continuing to
411	  review", partial findings with no verdict).
412	
413	**Required handling:**
414	
415	1. Do not interpret an incomplete result as approval, and do not interpret it as findings — `verdict-normalize` returns `incomplete` for exactly this case, and only `approved` exits the gate.
416	2. Recover best-effort, bounded:
417	   - **Code gates:** the recipe-code.md watch loop *is* the recovery path — the job id is
418	     known from launch, and `gate-wait <job-id>` / `result <job-id>
419	     --json` return the verdict whenever the detached worker finishes, no matter
420	     how many individual watch calls timed out along the way. If the watch cap
421	     passes with `.job.status` still `queued`/`running`, the worker is stalled
422	     or dead: run `status <job-id> --json` one final time, optionally
423	     `cancel <job-id>`, and stop — relaunch the review at most once, and only if
424	     the failure looked transient. If the job id was lost, find it again with
425	     `status --json`, whose snapshot exposes `running` (active jobs),
426	     `latestFinished`, and `recent` (each job carries `id` and
427	     `jobClass: "review"`) — there is no flat `jobs[]` array.
428	   - **Document gates:** the foreground `task` call returned without a verdict.
429	     Check `status --json` for a completed job holding the result
430	     (`result <job-id> --json`); if none, re-run the document review once with
431	     the explicit 600000 ms (10 minutes) timeout from gate-setup.md if the failure looked
432	     transient, otherwise surface it.
433	   - The authoritative signals everywhere are `.job.status` (`queued`/`running` = not done; `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled` = terminal) for job lifecycle, and the captured result file + `verdict-normalize` for the review outcome. The raw review text for reading findings remains at `.storedJob.result.rawOutput` or `.storedJob.result.codex.stdout`. Do not hand-roll a `sleep`-then-re-query loop; `status <job-id> --wait --json` is the condition-based primitive (2 s interval, 240 s deadline by default) and returns as soon as Codex is done; agents reach it through `gate-wait`, which applies it to every job of a gate in one call. A wait cycle is not a review round — it does not consume the §5 convergence/backstop budget.
434	3. If still incomplete after the bounded recovery, hand back to the user as
435	   "Codex review did not complete (still running / aborted before verdict)" —
436	   never silently pass. Like every other gate failure this degrades to "no Codex
437	   review," not "Codex approved."
438	   Before continuing past an unrecovered incomplete, record it durably (code
439	   gates with the range; document gates without):
440	
441	   ```bash
442	   bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/ungated-ledger" append --class incomplete-review --gate <spec|plan|task|final|adhoc> [--base <BASE sha> --head "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"] --status incomplete --gate-dir "$GATE_DIR" --note "review did not complete"
443	   ```
444	
445	The companion itself offers no working `--background` for `adversarial-review`;
446	the detached launch in recipe-code.md supplies the background path from the harness side.
447	A plain blocking call turns any harness timeout into an unrecoverable lost
448	review — that is why the detached launch is the required form, not an
449	optimization.
450	
451	Document gates (spec/plan) need none of this watch machinery: run `task` in
452	the foreground (gate-setup.md) with the explicit timeout and it blocks and returns the
453	verdict inline. Do not add
454	`--background` and do not poll — backgrounding a document review only replaces a
455	clean blocking call with a detached worker you then have to chase through
456	`status`/`result`. If you ever do need a job's terminal state, use
457	`bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/gate-wait" <job-id>` with `CODEX_PATH` exported (outside the shell sandbox), never a blind `sleep`.
458	
459	> **Red Flag — Never** treat an unfinished, timed-out, or "still verifying"
460	> Codex result as "no findings" / approval. Incomplete is not a pass. Recover via
461	> `status`/`result` or surface it — do not infer a verdict Codex did not give.
462	
463	> **Red Flag — Never** background a document review, and never `sleep`-then-poll
464	> for any Codex result. Foreground `task` returns the verdict inline; when a job
465	> genuinely needs awaiting, `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/gate-wait" <job-id>` returns the instant it is
466	> done. A blind wait-then-poll burns wall-clock and risks reading a verdict
467	> before it exists.
468	
469	> **Red Flag — Never** launch a code review and move on (or fall idle) while it
470	> runs. The recipe-code.md watch loop keeps a blocking `gate-wait` call in the
471	> foreground for the whole review — launch-and-forget hides that work is in
472	> flight and risks acting before the verdict exists.
473	
474	> **Red Flag — Never** launch `adversarial-review` without a passing `base-ref-ok`
475	> on the exact base you pass. A bad base does not fail fast — it orphans the
476	> review as `running` forever with no verdict.
477	
478	> **Red Flag — Never** derive approval yourself from raw companion output:
479	> only a `verdict-normalize` result of `approved` counts as approval. If the
480	> script says `incomplete`, there is no verdict, no matter how finished the
481	> raw text looks.
482	
483	===== gate-fix-loop
484	## 5. Fix-and-re-review loop (converge, then stop)
485	
486	After the first Codex review, every later round is a **re-review against known
487	state**, not a cold re-derivation. The loop ends as soon as the work is actually
488	done — it does not burn a fixed attempt budget.
489	
490	### Round ledger (re-review memory)
491	
492	Before re-running Codex (round 2+), write a small handoff file inside the
493	per-run `GATE_DIR` from §3 (e.g. `"$GATE_DIR/codex-round-ledger.md"`).
494	Do not paste it into your own context — hand it over as a file path. For each
495	completed round it records:
496	
497	- **Resolved** — each blocking finding and how it was addressed, with the fix
498	  commit/diff reference (code) or the spec/plan edit (documents).
499	- **Declined** — each finding you declined as *refuted* or *corrected* with file:line evidence, and each confirmed defect your human partner explicitly accepted as risk, in their own recorded words, labelled *accepted risk*; each with the explicit reasoning (the
500	  decision below to decline a finding, carried forward instead of lost).
501	- **Still open** — any blocking finding not yet resolved, and why.
502	
503	Each later round appends a new section; the ledger is the cumulative record.
504	
505	The round 2+ invocation has exactly two parts, in order: the round-aware preamble, which names the ledger path, and the §3 recipe's own focus string unchanged. The ledger file carries the findings, the fixes, and the diff references, so the focus string carries none of them — measured re-review focus strings that restated the ledger inline ran to a median of 464 words and a maximum of 35468. The preamble is:
506	
507	> This is re-review round N. The prior-round findings and how each was resolved
508	> or declined are in `<LEDGER_PATH>`. Confirm the resolved findings are actually
509	> fixed. Do not re-raise a finding listed as declined unless you can show the
510	> stated reasoning is wrong. You may raise any genuinely new **blocking
511	> (Critical or High)** finding — whether or not it is a regression — provided it
512	> is not already listed as resolved and not a declined item without a new
513	> argument. Do not raise new Minor (medium/low) findings on a re-review.
514	
515	The bar on re-review is "new and blocking," not "new and a regression": a
516	newly-noticed Critical or High issue is still blocking even if it predates round
517	1. What is excluded on re-review is Minor noise, not new blocking severity.
518	
519	If a re-review round returns new Minor (medium/low) findings anyway, they are
520	out of contract: record them in the round ledger as noted (and in the skill's
521	Minor ledger, if it keeps one), do not fix them in the loop, do not dispatch a
522	fix for them, and do not let them delay convergence. Only blocking findings
523	drive the loop.
524	
525	### Algorithm adjudication and lock (plan gate)
526	
527	Adjudicate the round-1 Algorithm Assessment immediately after parsing the
528	round-1 output and **before applying the loop's exit rule**, so an
529	`alternative-suggested` entry is never dropped by an early `approve` exit:
530	
531	- **Approve + no alternatives (or all declined):** record the lock(s), then
532	  exit as usual. A decline changes no plan content, so no re-review is needed;
533	  declines appear in the ledger and the §6 hand-back.
534	- **Accepted alternative:** revise the affected plan task(s) — keeping
535	  interfaces, steps, and cross-task references consistent — record the lock,
536	  then run **one normal re-review round** over the revised plan (assessment
537	  omitted, lock line present). A materially revised plan is never handed off
538	  without a confirming Codex pass. The loop then converges as usual within
539	  the existing backstop.
540	- **Needs-attention:** the normal fix loop runs anyway; adjudicate and lock
541	  alongside the round-1 blocking fixes.
542	
543	Ledger entry formats (one entry per assessed choice, so the round-2+ lock line
544	always has explicit referents):
545	- `Algorithm locked: <new> (was <old>) — <rationale>`
546	- `Algorithm locked: <original> — Codex suggested <alt>, declined: <reason>`
547	- `Algorithm locked: <choice> — assessed appropriate, no alternative suggested`
548	
549	On plan-gate re-reviews, append this line to the round-aware preamble and omit
550	the Algorithm Assessment section from the prompt:
551	
552	> Algorithm choices are locked per the ledger; do not re-open them absent
553	> a new blocking (Critical or High) defect in the locked choice — correctness,
554	> feasibility, or fit at the stated constraints and scale. Advisory preference
555	> or optimization alternatives remain locked.
556	
557	### The loop
558	
559	The loop's exit rule is mechanical: a round converges only when
560	`verdict-normalize` returns `"result":"approved"` for that round's captured
561	output. `blocking` continues the fix loop; `incomplete` follows §4b recovery
562	and never converges the loop by itself.
563	
564	0. Before composing ANY LOGICAL round (round 1 included), advance the
565	   mechanical counter ONCE with this gate's ceiling from the backstop
566	   table — a round-1 lens batch is one logical round: one `gate-round`
567	   call covers composing and launching every lens prompt in the batch:
568	
569	   ```bash
570	   bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/gate-round" "$GATE_DIR" --ceiling <4 for document gates, 3 for final and code-review-request gates> --gate <spec|plan|final|adhoc>   # SDD per-task gate instead: --consumed <the task's non-gate fix rounds so far, read off the ledger> --gate task
571	   ```
572	
573	   `"verdict":"proceed"` composes the round. `"verdict":"backstop"` means the ceiling is already spent: do NOT invoke Codex again for this gate — follow the backstop stop-condition below. A non-zero `gate-round` exit is an internal failure: treat it as `backstop` — do not invoke Codex for this round, and if backstop-round fixes ship, use the full append command written in the Backstop-hit stop-condition below (no `reminder` JSON exists on this path).
574	1. The approval set is every capture required for the latest round: round 1's set is every lens capture; a re-review round's set is its single capture. An empty capture set never approves. The round converges only when EVERY capture in the set normalized `"result":"approved"`, this round raised no blocking findings, and the round ledger has no still-open blocking findings. If converged → done; go to step 6.
575	2. Otherwise address each blocking finding: for a document, edit the spec/plan; for
576	   code, dispatch a fix through the skill's existing fix path (for SDD's per-task
577	   gate that path resumes the implementer per SDD's fix loop, not a fix subagent).
578	   Confirm before you fix. Every blocking finding is a claim about the change; read the cited code before acting on it. Each finding lands in exactly one state. **Confirmed** — the defect is real: fix it; a confirmed defect leaves the ledger only through a fix or through your human partner's explicit acceptance of the risk, recorded in the ledger with their words, and the controller does not accept risk on its own. **Declined** — reserved for two cases, each with file:line evidence in the ledger: *refuted*, the cited code does not do what the finding says; or *corrected*, the defect exists but not at blocking severity, or not in this change's scope, and the evidence shows why. A decline without evidence is a silent drop. **Unsettled** — you could not confirm or refute it: it stays blocking, so fix it defensively or carry it to the hand-back as unresolved. Uncertainty never clears a blocker. You MAY decline a finding on those terms, with explicit reasoning recorded in the ledger, instead of fixing it.
579	   Record resolutions, declines, and still-open items in the round ledger.
580	   After any code fix, re-run the same Claude reviewer gate before re-running Codex.
581	   For SDD per-task gates, that reviewer gate is SDD's scoped re-review.
582	3. Re-run the same Codex invocation (with the round-aware preamble and ledger
583	   path) over the updated artifact once the relevant Claude review gate is clean
584	   (for SDD per-task gates, once SDD's scoped re-review is clean).
585	4. **Stop when any holds:**
586	   - **Approved (converged):** EVERY capture required for the latest round normalized `"result":"approved"`, this round raised no blocking findings, **and** the round ledger has no still-open blocking findings. A round that normalizes to `approved` while the ledger shows an unresolved blocker has not converged (the blocker may predate this round); a round that normalizes to `blocking` has not converged regardless of ledger state — do not exit without a normalized approval.
587	   - **Backstop hit** — the per-gate round ceiling below is reached. Stop and hand back with any unresolved blocking findings listed; do not loop indefinitely. A blocking finding first raised IN the backstop round has no round left to confirm its fix, so choose its disposition deliberately instead of defaulting to a fix: **carry it to the hand-back as unresolved** — it stays blocking, ships no unverified change and buys no follow-on gate, and is usually the right call when the fix is not trivial; a confirmed defect leaves that list only through a fix or your human partner's explicit acceptance of the risk, recorded in the ledger in their words, never through a controller decline; **fix it and open the follow-on review now**, while the context is live; or **fix it and defer**, only after telling your human partner plainly that a blocking-severity fix rides unreviewed until that review happens. Fixes applied in the backstop round ship without a confirming Codex pass — flag them in the §6 hand-back as verified by the Claude reviewer and tests only, not re-reviewed by Codex. When backstop-round fixes ship, also record them durably using the `reminder` template from `gate-round`'s backstop output: `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/ungated-ledger" append --class backstop-fix --gate <task|final|adhoc> --base <task BASE sha> --head <head sha> --gate-dir "$GATE_DIR" --note "<one line>"` — and name the returned event id in the §6 hand-back. That append schedules a full follow-on gate over the recorded range rather than discharging one, so both fix paths cost the same extra gate and differ only in when it is paid.
588	If any stop condition conflicts with the mechanical exit rule, the mechanical rule governs: no normalized approved, no converged exit.
589	
590	### Per-gate round backstops
591	
592	| Gate | Recipe | Backstop |
593	|------|--------|----------|
594	| Spec / Plan (document gates) | task | 4 |
595	| SDD per-task (code gate) | adversarial-review | shares SDD's five-round per-task fix cap (see hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) — no separate Codex ceiling |
596	| Final / code-review requests (code gates) | adversarial-review | 3 |
597	
598	Document gates get 4 rounds (cheap: a text edit + a `task` re-run). Code gates
599	get 3 rounds (expensive: fix subagent + Claude-reviewer re-run + a fresh
600	`adversarial-review` per round) — except SDD's per-task gate, which has no
601	ceiling of its own: its rounds are fix-loop rounds and stop at the task's
602	shared five-round cap. Convergence usually stops the loop earlier; the
603	backstop is a true backstop, not the common exit.
604	
605	> **Red Flag — Never** invoke the companion for a review round without a `proceed` from `gate-round`
606	> for this `GATE_DIR`. The agent's own round count is not authoritative — the counter file is; a
607	> backstop verdict means the ceiling is spent no matter what your recollection says.
608	
609	## 6. Hand back
610	
611	Summarize concisely before returning to the skill's normal next step:
612	
613	- Codex verdict, the round count, and whether the loop exited by convergence or
614	  by hitting the backstop,
615	- what Codex flagged (by mapped severity),
616	- what was fixed,
617	- what was declined and why,
618	- any unresolved blocking findings if the backstop was hit,
619	- whether any fixes were applied after the last Codex round (backstop exits) —
620	  state explicitly that those fixes are not re-reviewed by Codex,
621	- any Minor findings noted but not fixed, including out-of-contract Minors
622	  raised on re-review,
623	- whether an incomplete result occurred and how it was resolved (recovered via
624	  `status`/`result`, or surfaced to the user),
625	- the review runtime: the codex-plugin-cc version (`CODEX_VERSION` from the §1
626	  preflight) and the Codex model and reasoning effort the reviews ran with — read
627	  `model` and `model_reasoning_effort` from
628	  `${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/config.toml`; the companion runs reviews at
629	  these config defaults.
630	
631	Then continue the skill (present to user / mark complete / finish branch).
632

18	
19	**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are: BLOCKED status you cannot resolve, ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.
20	
21	**After every context compaction:** Claude Code re-attaches this skill cut to its first 20,000 characters, which ends partway through the task loop, and a full Read you made before the compaction does not survive it. After each compaction, the first and every later one, Read this file in full before your next action (a dispatch, a ledger write, or the finishing steps), then the ledger, along with any other skill you are following whose re-attached copy is cut short.

119	## Setup
120	
121	Ensure the work happens in an isolated workspace: use
122	hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one.
123	Never start implementation on a main/master branch without your human
124	partner's explicit consent.
125	
126	Conversation memory does not survive compaction. In real sessions,
127	controllers that lost their place have re-dispatched entire completed task
128	sequences — the single most expensive failure observed. Track progress in
129	a ledger file, not only in todos.
130	
131	- Each plan owns a workspace: at skill start, run this skill's
132	  `scripts/sdd-dir PLAN_FILE` — it prints the plan's scratch directory
133	  under the user cache
134	  (`${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/hyperpowers/sdd/<per-repo-key>/plans/<plan-slug>-<hash8>/`),
135	  home to every artifact for THIS plan: ledger, briefs, reports, review
136	  packages, tier-skip summary. The cache is off any protected path, so
137	  writing there never triggers a permission prompt, and it is outside the
138	  working tree, so it can never be committed. Another plan's directory is
139	  never yours to read or write.
140	- Check for this plan's ledger at `<workspace>/progress.md` — this plan's
141	  workspace only, never a sibling's. The workspace is the plan's identity:
142	  `scripts/sdd-dir` maps a plan to ONE directory whatever path form you
143	  hand it, so a ledger sitting in YOUR workspace is this plan's progress
144	  even when its first line records the path in another form (relative vs
145	  absolute, or through a symlink). Resolve that line and compare the file
146	  it points to, not the string. Tasks with a `Task <N>: complete` line are
147	  DONE — do not re-dispatch them; resume at the first task without one. A
148	  task whose last line is a fix round is mid-loop: resume the loop at the
149	  next round. A task whose last line is its implementer identity is a
150	  dispatch in flight: do not re-dispatch — reconcile that agent first
151	  (list your live children, chase its report), resume it by the recorded
152	  id where your harness allows, and only if it cannot be recovered
153	  dispatch a takeover, recording the takeover's identity beside the
154	  original. A first line that resolves to a genuinely different plan
155	  file means this workspace is corrupt, not that you wandered into a
156	  sibling's: stop and surface it to your human partner rather than
157	  starting fresh on top of another plan's state.
158	- Create the ledger with its identity as the first line:
159	  `# SDD ledger — plan: <plan file path>`.
160	- The ledger is your recovery map: the commits it names exist in git even
161	  when your context no longer remembers creating them. After compaction,
162	  trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
163	- The workspace is scratch, not a deliverable. The Finish step deletes it
164	  once the final whole-branch review is clean; `scripts/sdd-dir` also
165	  reclaims sibling workspaces idle for 14+ days as a backstop for sessions
166	  that never reach Finish. It never reclaims the workspace you are using —
167	  every call refreshes it — so a resumed session always finds its ledger.
168	
169	Read the plan once, note its context and Global Constraints, and create a
170	todo per task where your harness surfaces todos — the ledger is the
171	progress record either way; todos mirror it, never replace it. Read the
172	plan's `**Spec:**` header and the spec file it names: the spec is the
173	binding authority the plan argues from, and conflicts inside the plan
174	resolve against it. A plan whose spec is `none` or unreachable gets a
175	ledger line saying so — without a spec, a conflict has no tiebreaker but
176	your human partner.
177	
178	Before dispatching Task 1, scan the plan once for conflicts, writing down
179	what you checked as you check it:
180	
181	- tasks that contradict each other or the plan's Global Constraints
182	- anything the plan explicitly mandates that the review rubric treats as a
183	  defect (a test that asserts nothing, verbatim duplication of a logic block)
184	
185	The scan's output is a table, not a verdict. One row for every pair of tasks
186	that share a file or an interface: the two tasks, what one produces against
187	what the other consumes, and what you found. One row for every task: whether
188	its own text agrees with itself — the tests it specifies against the code it
189	specifies, the files it creates against the files it later touches. "The scan
190	is clean" without those rows is not a scan you ran.
191	
192	Write the table to the ledger. Then present everything it surfaced to your
193	human partner as ONE batched question — each finding beside the plan text
194	that mandates it, asking which governs — before execution begins, not one
195	interrupt per discovery mid-plan. Each finding is a decision with
196	consequences downstream, so it gets the shape the brainstorming skill's
197	Deciding Together section describes: the conflict and what each resolution
198	costs in chat, then the selection widget to collect the answers. If the scan
199	is clean, proceed without comment. The review loop remains the net for
200	conflicts that only emerge from implementation.
